patch_description: Instead of the hierarchical group→node→GPU packing pipeline (which constrains experts to stay inside pre-packed groups and uses slow per-item Python loops), this approach solves the problem globally in two fully-vectorized phases per layer: (1) replica allocation — the redundant expert slots are assigned one-by-one to the logical expert with the highest per-replica load (weight/count), which minimizes the maximum per-replica load; (2) GPU packing — the expanded replicas are sorted in descending load and placed with LPT (Longest Processing Time first) greedy assignment onto the least-loaded GPU that still has capacity, which is the classical 4/3-approximation for balanced bin packing and directly minimizes the per-GPU load spread. Working entirely with numpy integer/float arrays (no per-item Python min() over packs, no torch sort round-trips to CPU inside loops) makes it dramatically faster, and removing the hierarchical group constraint improves global expert-level balancedness since hot experts can now be replicated across any GPUs.
